title: the Weeping Wood Rising
premise: Sable Sandoval has spent his life guarding the Weeping Wood, a valley where magic cannot enter and where he hides from a debt written into his blood: his mother sold his soul to the court beneath the mountain before he was born. When a dying courier gives him a map to that court, Sable learns the sale is due to be collected at the next dark moon. He ventures beyond the valley for the first time, guided by Wren, a memory-keeper who loved him once and paid for it with her own recollections of him. In the mountain's bone halls, Sable discovers he can reclaim his soul only by trading something equal—and chooses instead to shatter the ledger itself, freeing every soul held there, though it costs him all memory of the wood and of Wren. The book ends with Wren choosing to become his keeper in turn, teaching him who he was, love given freely against all duty.
about_author: Petra Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing estate ledgers and probate records, an obsession that seeps into her fiction's fascination with debts, names, and what can legally be owned. She writes from a rain-dark coastal town, where she claims the fog does most of her drafting.

chapters.title: The Gate That Stays Shut
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable tends the valley gate and its quiet wards, hiding the tremor in his own shadow that marks him as sold. A stranger crawls through the boundary—impossible, since magic cannot follow—dying, and presses a map into Sable's hands along with a warning: the collection comes at dark moon. Emotional beat: the terror of a hidden life ending.

chapters.title: What Wren Forgot
chapters.summary: Alternating Sable and Wren POV. Sable flees the valley with the map and meets Wren, a memory-keeper who traded away her memories of him to buy his mother's silence years ago; she helps him without knowing why she aches at his face. They cross a countryside where the court's collectors sniff for unpaid souls. Emotional beat: grief for a love neither can name.

chapters.title: The Ledger Beneath
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, with Wren captured mid-chapter. In the bone halls beneath the mountain, Sable confronts the Ledger-Keeper and learns the truth of his mother's bargain—and that reclaiming his soul requires a trade of equal weight. He offers himself fully, but sees Wren's name on a newer page: her payment bought less time than she knew. Emotional beat: duty curdling into defiance.

chapters.title: Rising
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, climax and resolution. At the dark moon, Sable refuses the trade and tears the ledger apart, unbinding every soul it holds as the court collapses around them; the price is his entire past, wiped clean. He wakes in the Weeping Wood knowing nothing, and Wren—keeper now of both their memories—begins telling him their story. Emotional beat: survival's cost answered by chosen love.
